messages:
hana: heads-up: sparrow-int8 canary produced well-formed JSON on most runs but we're seeing rare parse failures in the consumer that parses NDJSON lines. Root cause looks like unescaped control characters (0x1E, 0x00) sneaking into tool_call.args strings when tokenized/quantized. example payload excerpt below.

ryan: how rare? can you paste the raw line?

hana: ~0.15% of canary runs. raw NDJSON line received by consumer (showing non-printable as hex escapes):

`{"id":"r-73","tool_calls":[{"id":"t-3","name":"exec","args":"run\x1Erm -rf /tmp"}]}`

consumer treats NDJSON line-splitting by record-sep (0x1E) per our internal shim; that char inside args causes it to split mid-record and throws SchemaError: missing required field 'tool_calls[1]'.

marta: interesting. so the tokenizer/decoder is emitting U+001E in the middle of generated text? That's unusual since we typically escape control chars in the serializer. Is this introduced by quantized model or by a downstream byte-encoding pass?

diego: I reproduced locally by forcing int8 decode paths with FORCE_INT8_BUFFER=1 and enabling token sampler temperature 0.8. It seems when rerolling candidates during partial-retry we append raw byte sequences from the model output buffer that haven't been through our JSON-escape pass. So two-phase issue: model output may contain control bytes; serializer assumes all model bytes pass through an escaping filter but retries bypass it.

hana: repro script: eng-ml/canary-repro/ctrlchar-repro.sh (uses sparsify quant, --streaming=false to isolate single-line NDJSON). I'll upload gist.

ryan: immediate customer impact: any NDJSON consumer that uses RS (0x1E) splitting will mis-parse. We also saw a downstream log aggregator drop the event causing an SLI blip in last 24h. opsbot, did we get any infra alerts?

opsbot: alerting noted a consumer decode error spike at 2024-10-02T09:14:33Z tagged canary=sparrow-int8; ticket INF-3457 created.

marta: suggested fixes: 1) defensive: post-serializer sanitize pass that replaces control chars with escaped unicode sequences (e.g., \u001E -> "\\u001E") before NDJSON emit. 2) fix retry path so that any appended model buffer is always routed through same escape/serializer codepath. 3) model-side: add a tokenization banlist mapping for ILLEGAL_CONTROL -> escape tokens, but this is longer-term. 4) add unit test in streaming and non-streaming paths that injects control bytes and asserts final NDJSON parity.

diego: short-term mitigation: enable NDJSON-safe mode for structured-output routes for all int8/int4 canaries (sanitize at aggregator). Also increment telemetry metric structured_control_char_hit with tags {model, quant, canary_run}.

hana: agree. We should also add a canary-level linter that rejects any response containing record-sep or null bytes and fails the canary to prevent rollout.

ryan: what about escaping semantics? If we escape to unicode sequences consumers need to understand they'll see literal backslash-u sequences in args. Is that acceptable for tool args? Some downstream tools expect raw shell input.

marta: good point. For command/execution tools we should base64-encode args that contain binary/control bytes and annotate tool_call metadata with encoding: base64. That preserves fidelity and avoids ambiguous escapes. For most text usecases simple \uXXXX escaping is fine. We'll do heuristics: if bytes outside printable ASCII range are present, base64-encode.

diego: plan then: a) immediate aggregator sanitize that replaces 0x00..0x1F (except \n,\t) with unicode-escaped sequences; fail canary if any found (safe-mode), b) patch retry path to funnel buffers via same escape routine, c) add base64 fallback for tool args containing more than 2 control bytes, add tool_call.metadata.encoding=base64. d) telemetry and canary gating.

hana: I'll open PR for sanitizer + canary-linter and upload repro gist. diego will do retry-path patch. marta will draft base64 fallback RFC for review.

opsbot: created INF-3462 assigned to hana and diego; linked INF-3457. https://internal/ops/INF-3462 :white_check_mark:

ryan: nice. also create a docs blurb in devdocs under structured-output "Control chars and binary data handling" so onboarding engineers know encoding expectations.

hana: will add docs note. Thanks team :thumbsup:
